description: A hierarchical inference engine for frontier MoE models: hot experts on the GPU (CUDA, Vulkan), warm ones in RAM, cold ones streamed from NVMe. Written in C, runs on the hardware you already own.

latest_release.name: colibri v2.1.0
latest_release.body:
**Huge open models on the machine you already have**: on the CPU, on any GPU through Vulkan, on NVIDIA cards through CUDA. Pure C, one file per model family. 387 pull requests since v2.0.0, 208 of them from 35 contributors. GGUF files now run natively on every engine, read exactly as published. Four new models arrive, Mistral-Large-4 (1T) among them. CUDA gets device chains of its own and a routed-expert tier for every engine. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next runs a 256k context at the speed of 64k, an agent's turns read only what is new, and there is a new chat UI.

## Highlights - **GGUF on every engine.** `coli import` takes a GGUF where it lies and every engine runs it as published: no conversion, no second quantization, from IQ1_S to Q8_0, F16, BF16 and MXFP4, the same blocks and the same tokens on the CPU, Vulkan and CUDA. unsloth's Dynamic UD quants run as they are ([docs/gguf.md](https://github.com/JustVugg/colibri/blob/v2.1.0/docs/gguf.md)). - **New models.** Mistral-Large-4 (1T, 52B active: text, pictures, reasoning, tools), Muse Spark Open (816B), Flint (40B, 2.5B active), LFM3-VL-2B with its vision tower, and the published DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Kimi K3 GGUFs. - **CUDA.** Every layer of Qwen3.6, Qwen3.8 and OLMoE as one chain on the card, a routed-expert tier on the card for every engine, the dense matrices on the card for DeepSeek V4, V4.1, Kimi K3, GLM-5.3 and MiMo, and a GGUF's blocks on CUDA with the prompt on the tensor cores. - **Vulkan.** A model larger than the card keeps the experts the card cannot hold in a host pool in RAM, and the CPU computes them inside the device's frame while the card computes its own. Prompts on the matrix units, flash attention with windows and sinks, float16 KV mirrors. - **Long contexts and agents.** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next at 262,144 tokens: decode 9.6 to 45.7 tok/s, prompt 15.6 to 149. A short request between two turns (a title, a summary) parks the conversation instead of taking its state, on every engine: a Hermes Agent turn went from 86 s to 4.9 s. - **A new chat UI.** `coli ui`: reasoning in its own block, pictures, web search, a live map of the experts as they fire, a monitor, your models, and coding agents already pointed at colibri. Seven languages. - **Speculative decoding.** Qwen3.6's MTP head on every backend (`Q36_MTP=1`): decode 99.7-104.5 to 115.8-120.1 tok/s on CUDA, 83.2-83.8 to 99.9-109.3 on Vulkan; DeepSeek V4.1's DSpark head drafts as deep as its confidence says, behind a gate that skips the drafts that cannot pay. - **Memory.** KV caches in float16: GLM-5.3 at 131,072 tokens in 11.9 GB instead of 23.9. ## Measured on one 24 GB card An i5-13500 with 62 GB of RAM and an RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell SFF (24 GB, 70 W), each model served by `coli serve`: a fresh 450-token prompt, then a 128-token streamed answer, the request's HTTP included; the better of two runs, tok/s. | GGUF | CUDA prompt | CUDA decode | Vulkan prompt | Vulkan decode | CPU prompt | CPU decode | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M | 3,491 | 104.8 | 2,076 | 92.9 | 122.6 | 13.9 | | LFM3-VL-2B Q4_K_M | 12,317 | 235.1 | 8,174 | 214.1 | 286.5 | 34.5 | | OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct Q4_K_M | 10,418 | 354.6 | 6,867 | 299.4 | 279.9 | 47.4 | | LFM3-VL-2B F16 | 11,524 | 103.4 | 7,767 | 99.3 | 49.7 | 6.4 | | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ2_XS (68 GB: the experts the card cannot hold stay in RAM) | 217.1 | 51.4 | 214.3 | 50.6 | 38.3 | 9.3 | ## Bigger than the RAM, on the same machine Each model from its published GGUF; what neither the card nor the RAM holds comes from two NVMe drives. Tokens per second, from each model's page in `docs/`. | GGUF | size | backend | prompt | decode | |---|---:|---|---:|---:| | Inkling-Small UD-IQ2_XXS | 77 GB | Vulkan | 15.1-33.1 | 10.92-11.53 | | MiMo-V2.6-Flash Q2_K_S | 106 GB | Vulkan | 8.

detail.readme_excerpt:
Website · Discord · English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · Italiano · 日本語 · Bahasa Indonesia · Português (Brasil)

**Tiny engine, immense model.** colibri runs very large open models on the machine you already have. A mixture-of-experts model of hundreds of billions of parameters uses only a small part of itself for each token, so colibri keeps that part in RAM and reads the rest, the experts, from the disk when the model asks for them. Pure C, one file per model family, no GPU required. Thirteen engines run today. Ten are for language models: **GLM-5.2/5.3** (which also runs **Mistral-Large-4**), **GLM-5.3-Flash**, **Inkling**, **Kimi K3**, **DeepSeek V4 Flash**, **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash**, **MiMo-V2.6 Flash** (and Pro), **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next**, **Qwen3.6** (which also runs Qwen3-Coder, the dense Qwen3.8-27B, **Flint**, **Muse Spark Open** and **LFM3-VL**) and **OLMoE**. One draws pictures: **Qwen-Image-2.1**. Two answer decisions: **Laya** and **GLiNER2.5-Decide**, with a third decision model, **Clef**, on the Qwen3.6 engine. The language models also run from the GGUF files already published, read as they are ([GGUF](docs/gguf.md)), on the CPU, on any GPU through Vulkan and on NVIDIA cards through CUDA. [Which one for my machine](#which-model-for-my-machine) ``` $ ./coli chat colibri v2.1.0 · GLM-5.2 · 744B MoE · int4 · streaming CPU ✓ ready in 32s · resident 9.9 GB › ciao! ◆ Ciao! Come posso aiutarti oggi? ```


colibri is free and open source. If it has earned a place on your machine, a coffee helps pay for the next engine and the next speedup.

## Get started in one step You need a computer with **8 GB of RAM** at the very least (16 GB or more is better), **22 GB free on the disk** for the smallest model, and an internet connection. A graphics card is optional. **Windows** 1. On this page click **Code**, then **Dow
